title: Dilated eye exam
what: Drops are put in your eyes to make the pupils wide. Through them, the doctor can clearly see the retina, blood vessels, and the optic nerve.
why: For diabetes and high blood pressure, short-sightedness, flashes and floaters, worse vision, and at a routine check-up.
duration: the visit usually takes 40 to 60 minutes; the drops take 20 to 30 minutes to work
tell_doctor: If you have glaucoma, or were told you have a narrow angle in your eye
If you ever had attacks of eye pain with nausea

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: Do not drive after the exam. Your vision will be blurry for a few hours. Take a taxi or come with someone.

prepare.title: Contact lenses
prepare.text: Bring your lens case. Lenses are taken out before the exam.

prepare.title: Your plans
prepare.text: For a few hours after the exam, reading and looking at your phone are hard. Do not plan work with small print.

steps: Usually your vision and eye pressure are checked first
Drops are put in each eye
You wait 20 to 30 minutes while your pupils widen
The doctor shines a bright light into your eye through a lens or a device
You are asked to look up, down, and to the sides
feel: The drops may sting a little
The bright light is unpleasant, but it does not hurt
Afterwards your vision is blurry and light feels too bright
after: Blurriness and light sensitivity usually pass in 4 to 6 hours, sometimes by the evening
The doctor tells you the results right away
red_flags: Severe eye pain, redness, or a headache with nausea and rainbow rings around lights after the drops: see an eye doctor urgently or call emergency services

faq.q: How long do the dilating drops last?
faq.a: Usually 4 to 6 hours. For some people, until the evening or the next morning.

faq.q: Can I drive after a dilated eye exam?
faq.a: No. While your pupils are wide, your vision is blurry and light is dazzling. This is dangerous.

reminders.text: Dilated eye exam in 3 hours. Do not drive. A taxi home is best. Bring sunglasses.
